meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the VPSA-V1 unit
meta.scope: From the air intake F-100 and compressor K-100 through E-100, V-100, the adsorbers V-101A/B and the switching valves to the O2 buffer V-102 and the customer battery limit at XV-126 (off-spec vent XV-127); the vacuum system K-101, seal water and V-104 to the N2-rich buffer V-103 and the user battery limit at PV-133 / HV-136; the KS-140 sequencer, the SIS and the procedures. Utilities (instrument air, chilled water, power) are causes.
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: The unit is operated by trained staff at the design conditions. Instrument air, chilled water, seal water and power are available at start-up; the customer takes O2 at about 3 bar a. Instruments and relief valves are tested on the plan in the maintenance procedure.
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

N1.causes:
K-100 motor trip (fault library)
power failure
VSD fault
ESD
N1.cons: No air for the beds; if the cycle went on stepping the beds would only be evacuated; O2 production stops and the customer loses supply once the buffer is used.

N1.causes:
Intake filter F-100 plugging (fault library)
worn screw rotors (fault library)
hot ambient air (fault library) using up the speed margin
N1.cons: Less air per half cycle: lower production and higher power per Nm³ of O2; the customer is short when the speed reaches its limit.

N1.causes:
FIC-101 set point raised to make more O2 (fault library: production push)
FT-101 reading low
N1.cons: More N2 per half cycle than the beds can take: the N2 front leaves the bed top and off-spec O2 reaches V-102 and the customer.

N1.causes:
Filter element heavily loaded (dust storm, fault library)
element collapsed after a long overrun
N1.cons: Collapse of the element: dust and debris into K-100 (rotor damage) and on to the zeolite.

N1.causes:
Hot afternoon (fault library)
internal cooling of K-100 fouled
recirculation at high speed
N1.cons: Hotter air into E-100 and more load on the chilled water; rotor coating damage in the oil-free screw.

N1.causes:
Intake close to the N2-rich vents (PSV-103, HV-136)
vehicle exhaust or hydrocarbon vapour near the intake
higher humidity
N1.cons: N2-rich vent gas lowers the O2 in the feed (less production); hydrocarbons concentrate in the oxygen-rich zone of the beds and in V-102: ignition risk in oxygen service.

N1.causes:
Bearing or gearbox seal failure on the oil-free compressor
wrong machine or lubricant after maintenance
N1.cons: Oil films on the zeolite and in the product lines: fire or explosion in oxygen service at PV-122, FV-125 or V-102; loss of bed capacity.

N1.dev: Back-flow from V-100 through the stopped compressor
N1.causes:
K-100 trip or stop with V-100 at up to 5.5 bar a
no or failed non-return valve on the discharge
N1.cons: Screw driven backwards; V-100 depressurises through K-100 to the intake; dust blown back into the filter.

recs.text: Agree a back-up O2 supply with the customer (liquid-O2 tank and vaporiser with automatic change-over on low supply pressure), sized for a restart after a trip and for a cold start-up.
Confirm the K-100 package protections (discharge temperature, vibration, motor) and wire them to the DCS so they appear as the cause of a K-100 STOP / I-3 first-out.
Duplex intake filter F-100 with on-line change-over, and a PDI-100 high-high alarm before the element can collapse.
Limit the FIC-101 set point range in the DCS (operator range around design; higher only through an engineering review of the cycle) so production pushes cannot drive the N2 front through the beds.

Review the air-intake location: away from the PSV-103 and HV-136 discharges, the V-104 vent, vehicle routes and hydrocarbon sources; check the intake air for hydrocarbons where the product use requires it.
Oil-free certification of K-100 and a periodic oil-in-air check downstream of E-100; after any oil carry-over, a clean-for-oxygen inspection of the product side before restart.

Oxygen-compatibility review (materials, valve trims, velocity limits, adiabatic compression; ASTM G88/G94, EIGA Doc 13 / CGA G-4.4) of PV-122, FV-121, FV-125, XV-113/114/126/127 and V-102, and a clean-for-oxygen procedure after every intervention.
Confirm a non-return valve on the K-100 discharge (not shown on the screen P&ID) so V-100 cannot back-flow through the stopped compressor.
